name: Tear of Tilloa
summary: In Duskwood, the Tear of Tilloa grows on the Mistmantle estate near Darkshire. Its alchemical use draws interest from those seeking rare reagents.

sections.title: A Garden in the Gloom
sections.body: The Tear of Tilloa grows on the grounds of Stalvan Mistmantle’s estate outside Darkshire. Duskwood’s soil has turned hostile to wholesome vegetation, yet the small white flower persists among the shadowed plots. It grows rarely and in a secluded place, drawing those who seek uncommon reagents beyond lawful markets.

sections.title: A Concoction for the Nobles
sections.body: Beneath Stormwind’s streets, Zardeth of the Black Claw seeks the Tear of Tilloa to brew a draught for Lord Wishock. A member of the House of Nobles, Wishock threatens to investigate shadowy operations beneath the capital. Zardeth combines the flower with Musquash Root from beneath the Stonewrought Dam to make a brew meant to distract and incapacitate Wishock before an official probe can begin.

faq.q: Where does the Tear of Tilloa grow?
faq.answer: The flower grows on the outskirts of Darkshire in Duskwood, in the overgrown garden of the Mistmantle family estate.

faq.q: Who wants the Tear of Tilloa?
faq.answer: Zardeth of the Black Claw seeks the flower while operating covertly beneath Stormwind City, where he needs it for a special draught.

faq.q: What is the flower used for?
aliases: what does tear of tilloa do
faq.answer: The flower is combined with Musquash Root to make a brew intended to incapacitate Lord Wishock and silence his calls to investigate dark dealings beneath the capital.
Lord Wishock is a nobleman in Stormwind’s House of Nobles. After learning of subversive operations beneath the city, he began urging the council to investigate.

angles.text: As a herbalist, you may find the Tear of Tilloa growing in Duskwood’s blighted ground, far from the usual lush fields.
As a warlock, you may know the Tear of Tilloa as a reagent sought by occult operatives beneath the capital for brews meant to silence probing nobles.
